panels.description: Pages successfully fetched per second. Blue is the 5-minute smoothed average (steady-state read); green is the raw 1-minute rate (catches microbursts + dips). When green diverges sharply from blue, something just changed. Values on the Y axis are pages/sec. Source: rate(crawlrs_urls_fetched_total).
panels.title: Crawl Rate

panels.description: Share of attempts that completed cleanly over the last 5 minutes. Threshold markers: red <80%, yellow 80-95%, green >=95%. A sustained drop signals upstream blocks, broken hosts, or a regression in retry logic. Source: rate(crawlrs_urls_fetched_total) / (rate(urls_fetched) + rate(urls_failed)).
panels.title: Fetch Success Rate

panels.description: Cumulative successful fetches since process start. Resets on pod restart. Granular: shows 2 decimal places (e.g. 10.83 M). Source: sum(crawlrs_urls_fetched_total).
panels.title: Total URLs Fetched

panels.description: Workers currently in the running pool. Expected to track runtime.workers from config. A drop means the supervisor is rebuilding a crashed worker. Source: crawlrs_workers_active.
panels.title: Active Workers

panels.description: URLs marked permanently failed (retry budget exhausted). Background: green <=10, yellow 10-100, red >100. Source: crawlrs_dlq_size.
panels.title: DLQ Size

panels.description: How an average URL's wall-clock time decomposes across the six pipeline phases, stacked. politeness = robots/blocklist/circuit check. attempting = frontier lease + metadata claim. fetch = HTTP. extract = parse + adapter. store = Parquet/WARC write. commit = Postgres mark_succeeded + frontier ack. The tallest band is the phase eating most of the budget; thin it to speed up the whole pipeline. Source: rate(crawlrs_pipeline_phase_seconds_sum) / rate(crawlrs_pipeline_phase_seconds_count).
panels.title: Where does pipeline time go? (mean seconds per URL, by phase)

panels.description: URLs the politeness gate rejected over the last 5 minutes, broken down by why. `allow` is filtered out so the small disallow series stay visible. robots = blocked by robots.txt rule. blocked = host is in the blocklist. circuit = the host's circuit breaker is open. quota = per-host depth/url cap hit. Y axis is decisions/sec. Source: crawlrs_politeness_check_total.
panels.title: Politeness disallows (rate, by reason)

panels.description: URLs the runtime decided not to fetch. politeness_disallowed = caught by the gate (see panel left). depth_limit = discovered links past max_depth. Y axis is URLs/sec. Source: crawlrs_urls_skipped_total.
panels.title: URLs skipped (rate, by reason)

panels.description: Tail latency of each pipeline phase. Pair with 'Where does pipeline time go?' (mean) panel: mean tells you where average work goes, tail tells you where outlier URLs are getting stuck. P99 dashed; P95 solid. Source: histogram_quantile({0.95,0.99}, crawlrs_pipeline_phase_seconds).
panels.title: Pipeline phase tail latency (P95 / P99)

panels.description: Whole-pipeline duration per URL: claim through commit. Diverging P99 from P95 means one slow URL is monopolising a worker. Source: histogram_quantile(*, crawlrs_pipeline_seconds).
panels.title: Pipeline end-to-end latency (P50 / P95 / P99)

panels.description: HTTP status-class breakdown of fetch responses per second. 2xx = green (happy), 3xx = blue (redirects), 4xx = orange (client errors / host blocks us), 5xx = red (server errors). Stacked so the total and composition are visible together. Y axis is responses/sec. Source: crawlrs_fetch_response_total.
panels.title: Fetch responses by status class

panels.description: Categorical breakdown of failures recorded at the worker. too_many_requests = 429. service_unavailable = 503. connect_reset = TCP reset. timeout = exceeded request_timeout. other = transport/TLS/DNS. Y axis is failures/sec. Source: crawlrs_urls_failed_total.
panels.title: Fetch failures by cause

panels.description: Per-request fetch duration, broken down by request kind (page vs robots.txt). Robots fetches should be near-zero and cached; if they rise, the robots cache is broken. Page P99 above ~5s is your timeout-tail problem. Source: histogram_quantile(*, crawlrs_fetch_seconds).
panels.title: Fetch latency P50 / P95 / P99 by kind

panels.description: P95 + P99 of fetch stages. request = TTFB (DNS + TCP + TLS + headers); body = response streaming; total = full request. When total >> request the host streams slowly; when request alone is high DNS or TLS is sick. P99 dashed; P95 solid. Source: histogram_quantile({0.95,0.99}, crawlrs_fetch_stage_seconds).
panels.title: Fetch stage timing (P95 / P99) by kind + stage

panels.description: Distribution of fetched body sizes over the last 5 minutes. A jumping P99 means somebody started returning huge responses; that drives memory pressure and parse cost. Source: histogram_quantile(*, crawlrs_fetch_body_bytes).
panels.title: Body size distribution (P50 / P90 / P99)

panels.description: Average bytes per fetch, split by Content-Type bucket: html, non_html, unknown. Stacked area so you read both total bytes per second and composition mix at the same time. A drift toward non_html / unknown means crawl-budget is leaking on non-text resources. Source: rate(crawlrs_fetch_body_bytes_sum) / rate(crawlrs_fetch_body_bytes_count).
panels.title: Average body size by content type

panels.description: Per-shard backlog of URLs that have crossed the wake-time and are eligible for workers. A growing queue on one shard with the others idle means a hot host is monopolising that shard. Source: crawlrs_frontier_ready_length.
panels.title: Frontier ready queue by shard (top 10)

panels.description: How `Frontier::claim` calls resolve. claimed = worker got a URL to fetch (the healthy outcome). empty = queue was empty (we have nothing to do; idle). empty_hint = queue empty but a wake-time is coming soon (politeness-bound). error = Redis call failed. A growing `empty` rate with `claimed` collapsing means seeds are exhausted or the frontier is starved. Y axis is claims/sec. Source: crawlrs_frontier_claim_total.
panels.title: Frontier claim outcomes

panels.description: Every URL the parser discovers is offered to the per-shard bloom filter. `new` URLs go into the work queue. `duplicate` URLs were already seen (this run or any prior run) and are silently dropped. A healthy dense crawl has roughly 80-95% duplicates: most pages share outbound links. If `new` collapses to zero while you're still seeding, the bloom may have filled up (false-positive rate climbed past acceptable). Y axis is submits/sec. Source: crawlrs_frontier_bloom_total.
panels.title: URL dedup: new vs already-seen

panels.description: Share of robots.txt requests served from the in-process LRU + Redis cache (no network fetch). When `obeyRobotsTxt: false`, robots.txt is never fetched - both hits and misses stay at zero, the ratio is undefined, and we display `robots off`. When enabled, you want >=90%: a low hit rate means the cache TTL is too short. Source: rate(robots_cache_hits) / (rate(hits) + rate(misses)).
panels.title: Robots cache hit rate

panels.description: In-memory bytes each shard's writer is buffering before its next rotation. Buffers grow as the shard accumulates fetched bodies; they drop to ~zero each time the writer flushes (size cap / row cap / time cap). A shard that keeps climbing without flushing means rotation thresholds are too loose for its throughput - it'll OOM eventually. A shard that stays at zero hasn't written anything yet. Source: crawlrs_store_buffer_bytes.
panels.title: Store buffer bytes (top 10 shards)

panels.description: Smoothed outstanding pool checkout requests, by adapter. The raw value is bursty (workers spike checkouts to 5-10 and drop to 0 in milliseconds), so we average over 1 minute for readability. If this line sits above 0 sustained, the pool is undersized for the worker count. Frontier (Redis), Politeness (Redis), Metadata (Postgres) each have their own pool. Source: avg_over_time(crawlrs_*_pool_pending[1m]).
panels.title: Connection pool pending checkouts (1-min average)
Parquet files closed (lifetime)
panels.description: Cumulative count of Parquet files that have been flushed and closed since process start. Each closed file represents one row group (default ~10K rows) of fetched pages written to disk. New files are opened automatically when the previous one fills its row cap; this counter increments once per close-and-reopen event. The sparkline behind the number shows WHEN those rotations happened: a flat horizontal line means no files have rotated recently (in-progress files are still accumulating in the buffer above). Source: sum(crawlrs_store_rotation_total{format="parquet"}).
Time spent in lol_html parse + any registered SiteAdapter::extract. Parse is single-threaded per worker and CPU-bound; large pages drive P99. Source: histogram_quantile(*, crawlrs_parse_seconds).
panels.title: Parse latency (P50 / P95 / P99)

panels.description: Tail latency per write call to the configured stores. P95 solid, P99 dashed. Diverging P99 usually means rotation flushes; sustained high P95 means the object_store backend is slow. Source: histogram_quantile({0.95,0.99}, crawlrs_store_write_seconds).
panels.title: Store write latency P95 / P99 by format

panels.description: P95 time per metadata-ledger operation. mark_attempting drives the `mark` pipeline phase. mark_succeeded drives `commit`. mark_failed and mark_permanently_failed only fire on failures. Sustained P95 above ~50ms usually means the Postgres pool is contended or a query is missing an index. Source: histogram_quantile(0.95, crawlrs_metadata_query_seconds).
panels.title: Postgres query latency P95 by op

panels.description: Per-second rate of URL outcomes, stacked. Companion to the Fetch Success Rate gauge: the gauge tells you the headline %, this tells you where the rest is going. Green band = succeeded; red = failed (any kind); yellow = skipped (politeness / depth). Source: rate(crawlrs_urls_{fetched,failed,skipped}_total[1m]).
panels.title: Outcome mix (succeeded / failed / skipped, stacked)

panels.description: Total failures by cause over the dashboard's selected time range. Counts (not rates), so a spike of TLS errors that happened an hour ago is visible. Use to drill in when 'Fetch failures by cause' shows a non-zero category and you want exact numbers. Source: increase(crawlrs_urls_failed_total[$__range]).
panels.title: Failure attribution (counts over selected range, top 20 by kind)
